examined by us, the Company has been regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues including
Goods and Services tax, Provident Fund, Employees’ State Insurance, Income Tax, Sales Tax, Service
Tax, duty of Customs, duty of Excise, Value Added Tax, Cess and any other statutory dues applicable
to it with appropriate authorities;
 There were no undisputed amounts payable in respect of Goods and Service tax, Provident Fund,
Employees’ State Insurance, Income Tax, Sales Tax, Service Tax, duty of Custom, duty of Excise, Value
Added Tax, Cess and any other statutory dues in arrears as at 31st March, 2023, for a period of more
than six months from the date they became payable except for provident fund amount of Rs.0.45
Lakhs not deposited on account of non – linking of employee Aadhar details in the respective portal

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Adjudicating Authority – Commissioner, CGST & Central Excise, Mumbai Central, vide Order dated 15/07/2026, has confirmed a service tax demand of Rs. 2,60,07,500/-, along with applicable interest and an penalty of Rs. 2,60,07,500/-, in relation to the proposed sale of the 14th, 15th and 16th floors of Ruby IT Park to Shreem Corporation Ltd. (now Rajput Retail Ltd.) in 2012 and received Advance sum of Rs. 101 Crs. During the hearing the Company had contended that the advance of Rs. 101 Crores was received only after issuance of the Part Occupation Certificate for the said floors and, therefore, the transaction was not liable to service tax. However, the Adjudicating Authority rejected the Company's contention and passed the aforesaid Order
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Show cause notice issued to the Ruby Mills Limited in respect of Service Tax by the Commissioner CGST& C.Ex. Mumbai Central
tax_litigation.status: The Company is in consultation with its Advocates and Tax Consultants and shall take appropriate legal steps, including filing an appeal before the appropriate Appellate Authority.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: GST Tran 1 Credit Order in Original was passed on 3rd February 2025 wherein the department had demanded ineligible Transitional credit amounting to Rs. 1.16, thereby a demand of Rs. 1.16 crores with interest & penalty. The Company could not avail amnesty & thus has on merit filed the appeal within time against the order on 6th May, 2025. The hearing was conducted on 09/10/2025 our representative Mr. Samir Kapadia was present and argued on behalf of the Company, we have to submit necessary documents in this regard by 08/11/2025.The OIA allowed the company's Appeal partially for Rs. 91 Lacs by the Commissioner. The Company is filing appeal with GSTAT for balance of Rs. 26 Lacs.
